lines.text: Ziklag was ash before David even got close enough to call out any names.
His wives were gone. His sons were gone. And the men who'd just lost everything too started talking about ending him instead.
He didn't argue with their grief. He encouraged himself in the Lord — then asked the only question that mattered: shall I pursue?
Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.
So he ran after what was stolen — not alone, not quietly, not waiting for anyone's permission to want it back.
Whatever your Ziklag burned down, the same God is still saying pursue — and still promising all.

title: Word and Faith Network
subtitle: Pursue, Overtake, Recover All
story: A burned-out camp smolders into night as a grieving man kneels under a single shaft of light to ask God one question, then runs hard across a torch-lit dusk wilderness after what was taken - arriving at a gold sunrise where the flock is walked back in and nothing is missing. A visual telling of David at Ziklag (1 Samuel 30): ash, inquiry, pursuit, and a dawn where nothing is lacking.
